rows.evidence: Q1: Methods/Table 2 - the authors run 688 LPJmL simulations of their own (water management and climate scenarios). Q2: Section 3.2, Fig 5(b), Fig 4 - irrigation transition scenarios ('best practice' with drip where applicable, 'all drip') together with SMC cut consumptive irrigation losses by 24/48/85% and reduce global withdrawal from 2507 to 2071/1248/808 km3; model baseline is calibrated to FAO yield statistics and withdrawals are compared with FAO/other estimates (sections 2.2, 3.6). Q4: Sections 2.1.4, 3.1, 3.2 - the model explicitly simulates the intermediate variables (soil evaporation, interception, conveyance/application losses, transpiration coefficient rising from 42% to 49-61%) through which drip/sprinkler save water. Q5: Figs 2, 4, 5(b), section 3.3 - results reported at basin level across many climates/regions (Middle East, Asia, North/Central America, SSA) and 12 crop types, with spatial maps. Q6: Sections 3.1-3.3, Table 3 - effects reported at basin and global scale, accounting for downstream return flows. Q8: Sections 2.2, 2.1.5, 3.6 - nutrient limitation not represented; 'all drip'/'max' scenarios are biophysical limits not feasible targets; groundwater/diversion contributions not quantified; upstream improvements reduce return flows downstream; land use fixed after 2005; current adoption hard to quantify.
rows.notes: Doubt on Q2: the drip-specific water savings are hypothetical scenario outputs never compared with observations of actual drip adoption; only the baseline (yields vs FAO, withdrawals vs AQUASTAT/other estimates) is checked, and 'ambitious' combines drip with sprinkler. Q3 no: single modeling method. Q7: conditions ('drip where applicable', crop suitability) are design assumptions; need for institutional regulation of reallocations is a general recommendation. Q9: water-saving results given as point values, no dispersion; GCM ensemble applies to climate projections and only means/medians are reported.

rows.evidence: Q1: Methods/Table 2 - the authors run 688 LPJmL simulations of their own.
rows.notes: The study does not report any result on river flows or aquatic ecosystems. It shows reduced irrigation withdrawals and non-productive losses, but saved water is rerouted to irrigation expansion so consumptive use actually rises (Table 3: 1268 to 1515 km3 in 'ambitious'), and it notes that upstream irrigation improvements can reduce return flows and runoff downstream (section 3.6). Environmental flow requirements are only mentioned as something to respect in the Discussion. The withdrawal reduction is at most a precondition of enhanced river flows, so upstream is set true.

rows.evidence: Q1: Methods/Table 2 - 688 own LPJmL model runs. Q2: Section 3.3, Fig 5, Table 3 - irrigation improvements ('best practice': drip where applicable plus sprinkler; 'all drip') with expansion using saved water raise global kcal production by 7/26/43%; crop yields calibrated to FAO national statistics (section 2.2) and simulated yield gains compared with case-study ranges (section 3.6). Q4: Sections 2.1.4, 3.2, 3.3 - model simulates the mechanism: saved non-beneficial consumption (evaporation, conveyance losses) and higher transpiration, with saved water expanding irrigated area (297 to 642 Mha). Q5: Fig 5(b), section 3.3, 3.6 - basin-level results across regions (Middle East, Asia, Central/North America; flat potentials in SSA) and 12 crop types. Q6: Sections 3.1-3.3, Table 3 - results at basin and global scale with downstream accounting. Q7: Sections 2.1.4, 3.3, 3.6 - expansion gains require available rainfed cropland within the basin (some basins lack it so not all saved water is used) and only non-beneficially consumed water can be reallocated because return flows are crucial downstream. Q8: Sections 2.2, 2.1.5, 3.6 - no nutrient limitation in model; 'max'/'all drip' not feasible targets; WH suitability possibly exaggerated; groundwater contributions not quantified; land use fixed; sowing dates fixed.
rows.notes: Doubt on Q2: the 26% figure is a scenario output for a hypothetical drip/sprinkler transition not validated against observed adoption outcomes; only the baseline and WH/SI gains are compared with observations. Q3 no: single model. Q9: the 26% result is a point estimate without dispersion; the 20-GCM ensemble is used for climate projections but Table 4 reports only means/medians, no range or spread.

notes: Full text appears complete (supplementary figures S1-S5 not included). Global process-based modeling study (LPJmL); drip is one component of the irrigation transition scenarios ('best practice' mixes drip and sprinkler; 'all drip' is a biophysical-limit scenario).
